hints.title: Bounded Power Exponentiation
hints.text: Generate powers of x and powers of y as long as they remain strictly below bound.

hints.title: Degenerate Base Termination
hints.text: When x equals 1 or y equals 1, only power 1^0 = 1 is distinct; stop advancing that base after the first iteration.

hints.title: Deduplicated Set Collection
hints.text: Initialize powers_x with [1]. While x > 1 and powers_x[-1] * x < bound, append powers_x[-1] * x. Do identical for powers_y with base y. Sum every pair from powers_x and powers_y that is <= bound into a set and return sorted list.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterating up to bound naively wastes time testing integers that cannot be formed as sums of powers.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since powers grow exponentially, at most ~20 powers exist for any base >= 2, making the nested loop tiny.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate must carefully handle bases x = 1 and y = 1 to prevent infinite loops.
complexity.notes: For x = 1 and y = 1, the only candidate is 1 + 1 = 2.
